description.narrative: ASEAN-Australia Political-Security Partnership (APSP) supports ASEAN leadership and centrality in addressing regional political-security challenges. The program engages ASEAN sectoral bodies, the ASEAN Secretariat and ASEAN-led mechanisms, along with Australian Government agencies, in program activities such as regional dialogues, workshops, capacity building and research. The program focuses on policy areas that reflect priorities of both ASEAN and Australia including maritime security, cybersecurity, women, peace and security, transnational crime and conflict prevention.

description.narrative: APSP supported improved governance in ASEAN and Southeast Asia, strengthened the ASEAN-Australia relationship, and promoted multiple stakeholder cooperation. APSP worked with the ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime to strengthen cooperation across ASEAN through a counter terrorism workshop on community resilience and countering radicalisation, which brought together ASEAN and community stakeholders to produce a compilation of good and promising practices. APSP strengthened ASEAN engagement with Australian agencies (DFAT, AFP, AGD, AUSTRAC and e-Safety), including convening a workshop on addressing cybercrime threats. APSP supported strengthening the ASEAN Secretariat through a series of capacity building workshops on sensitive political security issues.

APSP worked with ASEAN Member State champions to build new areas of ASEAN-Australia cooperation and enhance regional stability by strengthening the ASEAN-led regional architecture in the political-security space. During the reporting period, APSP delivered 15 ASEAN-Australia activities in the areas of conflict prevention, maritime security, cybersecurity, cybercrime, dis/misinformation, transnational crime, and women, peace and security. ‍ An evaluation found that these activities had “significantly enhanced engagement between ASEAN and Australian agencies”; and had “positively contributed to regional stability and trust through enhanced coordination among law enforcement officials”, and “enhanced ASEAN cross-sectoral linkages.” These activities would not have occurred without APSP implementation and contributed directly to regional coordination and knowledge exchange on these issues. As an example, APSP delivered a large-scale ASEAN-Australia Track 1.5 Workshop on Conflict Prevention, Crisis Management, and the ASEAN-led regional architecture, bringing together officials from all East Asia Summit countries to discuss ASEAN’s role in conflict prevention. This elevated ASEAN centrality on conflict prevention, and resulted in a concrete set of recommendations, which ASEAN agreed to elevate to Senior Officials level in 2025.

ASEAN-Australia Political-Security Partnership supports ASEAN to address transnational political-security issues and facilitates engagement between Australian and ASEAN agencies. During the reporting period, APSP completed ten activities on maritime security, cybercrime, women, peace and security (WPS), counter-terrorism, and transnational crime, engaging sixteen ASEAN and eight Australian entities. APSP’s support on maritime issues, such as UN Law of the Sea training for ASEAN, was recognised in the Melbourne Declaration at the ASEAN-Australia Special Summit in March 2024, including at ASEAN’s Track 1.5 activity on Maritime Cooperation. APSP contributes to the ASEAN-Australia Work Plan on Combatting Transnational Crime and is the only support mechanism for three of the four areas under the Work Plan: counter-terrorism, illicit drugs, and cybercrime. APSP’s support for the ASEAN WPS High Level Dialogue advocated inclusion of Australia as observer to the ASEAN WPS Advisory Group, validating Australia’s reputation as key WPS partner.

ASEAN-Australia Political-Security Partnership supports strengthening inclusion practices in ASEAN’s counter-terrorism workstream by implementing cross-sectoral Australia-ASEAN workshops in partnership with Indonesia. Australia has worked with the Indonesian National Counter Terrorism Agency to organise two ASEAN-Australia Counter-Terrorism Workshops, and is working towards another two. During the reporting period, APSP worked with Indonesia to implement the second workshop, focused on countering violent extremism, hate speech and disinformation online (January 2024, Bali). The workshop provided a platform to exchange information among seven ASEAN sectoral bodies responsible for transnational crime, information, digital, human rights, youth, education, and women; as well as representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations, ASEAN Disability Forum, and social media platforms. The workshop produced a report compiling key challenges, good practices, and recommendations, highlighting the importance of multiple stakeholder cooperation to building community resilience. APSP will continue to support ASEAN’s efforts in this area.

In November 2023, the ASEAN-Australia Political-Security Partnership together with the Australian National Centre for Ocean Resources and Security (ANCORS), delivered capacity building training on the UN Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Officials from all ASEAN Member States and the ASEAN Secretariat. were involved, bringing together 65 officials (32 women, 33 men) working on maritime security policy from all ASEAN Member States, Timor-Leste, and the ASEAN Secretariat, to enhance their knowledge and understanding of UNCLOS. There was strong positive feedback about the training with 97 per cent of participants indicating they found the training useful. At the suggestion of participating officials, a second round of similar training is currently being developed.

The ASEAN-Australia Political Security Partnership (APSP) supported the second iteration of the Law of the Sea Training for ASEAN Member States and ASEAN Secretariat officials, delivered by the Australian National Centre for Ocean Resources and Security (ANCORS) in Jakarta, December 2024. The training included 44 officials (19 female, 25 male) from all 10 ASEAN Member States, Timor-Leste and the ASEAN Secretariat and aimed to enhance participants knowledge and understanding of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The training incorporated new topics suggested by ASEAN including submarine cables, blue economy, and labour inspection and laws related to the fishing sector. ‍ The program continued supporting the annual Expanded ASEAN Maritime Forum (EAMF), an ASEAN-led track 1.5 forum on maritime issues involving East Asia Summit (EAS) participating countries. As requested by Lao PDR, the 2024 ASEAN Chair, APSP funded the participation of regional academics to present policy briefs, including one on fostering blue economy by the Australian academic, at the 12th EAMF in Vientiane, November 2024.

The ASEAN-Australia Political-Security Partnership supported the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) priorities of ASEAN Women for Peace Registry (AWPR). APSP facilitated the participation of AWPR members at the ASEAN WPS High Level Dialogue in July 2023, hosted by Indonesia. APSP organised a knowledge sharing session on the role of civil society in WPS implementation between AWPR and the Australian WPS Civil Society Coalition in the sidelines of the Dialogue, followed by an AWPR drafting session on advancing the ASEAN WPS agenda. APSP also supported WPS and cybersecurity priorities of other ASEAN women’s rights bodies, namely the ASEAN Committee on Women (ACW) through the ASEAN Gender Mainstreaming Conference and the ASEAN WPS High Level Dialogue; and the ASEAN Commission on the Promotion and Protection of the Rights of Women and Children (ACWC)’s Regional Dialogue on Child Online Protection in September 2023.
